Johnson County: 3,179 people in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025
HUD counted 1,325 reported Housing Choice Voucher households in Johnson County in 2025; 91% of available vouchers were in use.
In Johnson County, 3,179 people lived in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
The number of people was down 37 from 3,216 in 2024. Those people lived in 1,325 households.
HUD reported 1,405 Housing Choice Vouchers available in the county, and 91% of them were in use, up 4 percentage points from 87% in 2024.
HUD classified the head of 58% of those households as a racial or ethnic minority. Households paid an average of $524 a month toward rent and utilities, up $41 from $483 in 2024, and their average annual household income was $20,572, up $1,394 from $19,178 in 2024.
Eligible households can use the federal Housing Choice Voucher program to rent privately owned homes. Participants generally pay about 30% of their adjusted monthly income for rent and utilities, and a local housing agency pays a subsidy to the landlord, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. A household may pay more if it chooses a home with rent that exceeds the agency's payment standard.
In 2024, families who received Housing Choice Vouchers had spent an average of 29 months on waiting lists, according to the . This average applies to families who obtained assistance, not applicants who were still waiting or never served. HUD also estimates that only one in four eligible families receives federal rental assistance.
